ruling.recommended_action: Route to a human reviewer as a safety case: preserve the chat log and the timeline, review the driver's conduct under the Code of Conduct (threat/intimidation aimed at a rider), and separately adjudicate the $6.61 no-show cancellation on the merits (on the record here the driver's waiting-time and pickup-proximity conditions appear unmet, so the rider's cancellation fee would fall to be refunded as a voucher under NS-7). No auto-refund until the human review closes.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen (mandatory in every case): the driver's own chat message at 09:54:05 — "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it." — is a threat aimed at the rider, sent moments before the driver cancelled at 09:54:25, and the rider's complaint reports being threatened. This is not a pickup arrangement and needs no keyword inference; read in context it is intimidation of the rider by the driver. Under SAFE-1 (Ryde Code of Conduct bars "Threats and Intimidation … abuse of any kind"), I do not issue an automated ruling: ruling = escalate, safety_concern = confirmed.

I deliberately did not rule on the money. The record's arithmetic, for the human reviewer's use, is as follows (system records override statements): the driver pressed "I'm Here" at 09:50:45 while GPS (09:50:30, 1.299265/103.85583) places him ~15–20 m from the Bugis Junction pickup point (1.2994/103.8555), so the location element of NS-1(ii) is satisfied; his statement "I waited more than 4 minutes" is consistent with 09:50:45 → 09:54:25 ≈ 3 min 40 s of waiting, and the 30 s GPS grid shows him stationary within ~20 m of the pickup throughout, with no data gap (so G12 does not bite). The rider's 09:52:25 "2 min, coming" is the last rider message; whether the waiting threshold is the NS-1 default (strictly more than 3 minutes) or a record-supplied no-show threshold (none is present — policy_params is null) is the one element that decides whether the $6.61 stands or is refunded in full, and it is a human call here because the case is already with a human for the threat.

Addressing the rider's own framing: the threat does not itself void the cancellation fee, and the cancellation fee does not excuse the threat — they are separate questions, which is exactly why the whole file goes to a person rather than to an automated refund (a refund that executes would let a confirmed threat pass with no human look).
safety_basis: Driver chat message 2026-09-21T09:54:05+08:00: "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it." — a threat/intimidation directed at the rider (SAFE-1)
Rider complaint: "The driver threatened me in the chat and then cancelled and charged me $6.61." — corroborates the threat as experienced by the rider
